text: The five template operations of this story are the TSD P6 T-A.1 rows API-P6-003 to API-P6-007 under /admin/templates on base /api/recovery/comms/v1, and the legacy /templates paths of RWB-E1-034 are the legacy names only.
why: The legacy story and the TSD name the same five operations differently and the sources do not reconcile them; the TSD outranks the story on source precedence and the checks fix /admin/templates for this service.
read: TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2; Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence and R4 naming
confirm: The rwb-comms tech lead confirms the five paths when the rwb-comms OpenAPI document is baselined.
impact: The screen and the tests call /admin/templates; a consumer built on the legacy /templates path would need a rewrite before the first consumer signs off.

text: No set-current operation is built: 'set current' in legacy AC2 is read as the approve action, and the current version of a template code and language on a date is the Approved version with the latest valid from on or before that date, derived on read.
why: The target contract has five template operations and none sets a version current, and no source states a set-current operation, its guard or its refusal.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-034 AC2 and section 4 step 7; TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1

impact: A version with no approver can never become current; the refusal text MSG-P6-005 is kept and is answered by the approve operation with status 422.

text: The allowed body file type list stays DOCX and the size limit stays 10 MB for Epic 1, both read as configuration (rwb.comms.template.allowed-types and rwb.comms.template.max-size-mb) until a source fixes them.
why: The legacy story marks the size limit assumed and no source names the allowed list, the limit or its owner.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-034 sections 8 (BR8) and 13; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1
confirm: The configuration owner confirms the list and the limit before the first SIT run and before the file upload is opened to users.
impact: A file type or a size outside the configured values is refused with 415 MSG-P6-010 and nothing is stored; no Java code holds either value.

text: The template body is stored write-once in this service's own Blob container and named by body_ref; no rwb-document contract is consumed for it in wave 1, and the container moves to a document-hub object through the rwb-document contract once that contract names one.
why: The Ownership Map gives the document entities to P5 rwb-document while the legacy story stores the body through the ACE storage pattern, and no source states which holds a template body.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-034 sections 3 and 13; TSD P6 Communications v2 T3.1 DF-REF-050; Ownership Map v1 template and merge_field rows
confirm: The solution architect confirms the container when the rwb-document contract of P5 is baselined.
impact: No P5 dependency is declared in wave 1 and body_ref stays a claim-check reference; a later move changes the TemplateBodyStore and no template row.

text: In the target rwb-comms never sets, changes or holds a retention class, a retention period or a disposal: the class, its list, the class per document type, the period and the disposal or extension decision are P5 rwb-document's (retention_rule, retention_action, JOB-17 and NFR-028 with DL26), and this legacy key keeps only the closure gate of R-WO-47 and R-WO-48. The service reads the class of every notice document on the rwb-document contract, records the coverage as the local decision record of decision code D9 with rule R-WO-47 or R-WO-48 and the rule version in force, and where a class is absent it holds the closure and asks for the Document Hub task; the class read is a consumed and faked row until P5 publishes the operation and the C row is added to RWB-P6-E4042-APP.
why: The story is a module P6 story by its own header and the ownership map puts the retention tables and the retention run on P5 rwb-document, while both slices of this key carry an empty contract dependency list; the class cannot be set or copied without breaking the single-owner rule of DP-01 and without a source for the class codes.

The path is fixed by D-RCV-60 in RWB-P6-E4042-CON because no source names a retention operation, the five elements are the ones the legacy Data table and the notice contract already name, and the field types, an optional class code and the page shape are settled in the baseline review with the gateway-bff and rwb-document owners.

text: The missing-class outcome is sent to rwb-case as one case fact carrying the case ID and the reason code RETENTION_CLASS_MISSING of R-WO-48, and rwb-case holds the closure, raises the Document Hub task and owns its 5 working-day timer. The fact is one hop on the rwb-case contract, it is consumed and faked in RWB-P6-E4042-CON with a placeholder on its body, and a refused or late answer leaves the decision unrecorded and the closure unconfirmed, because a class is never assumed present.

text: The Movement resource carries seven fields: id, noticeId, documentId, movedAt, fromLocation, toLocation and heldBy from the legacy data table, plus the seventh field the legacy data calls and 1 more, which stays the placeholder until the P5 document hub publishes its custody contract. The request carries document_id, moved_at, from_location, to_location and held_by, all required, with the document_id equal to the document reference of the notice. The types and required flags of the seven fields are the owner definition where it gives them and the placeholder elsewhere, and held_by is an organisational role, a team or a location and never a person. The notice keeps the identifier of the latest movement in a nullable column added by one per-service Flyway step in rwb_comms, named by the baseline.
why: The legacy data table names six fields and says and 1 more, the P6 data model has no custody object and no type for it, and the whole table definition belongs to the P5 document hub; the notice-side reference column is named by no source and is needed for the read of the contract.

text: The decision record of a movement is written before the change through the local decision-record library and the shared topic, with the record reference, the case, the notice, the document, the movement date, the from and to locations, the holder, the decided-at and the chain of the library; the decision code and the rule id of a custody movement stay the placeholder of the decision owner and no value is invented. text: A movement is accepted only when the notice is in the states of the parameter rwb.comms.custody.eligible-states, whose value is set at the baseline review, carries the document reference of the original, and the case is not under legal hold under R-UNI-20; a case that has closed refuses the movement on the consumed CaseStateChanged fact of the catalogue. A notice outside the parameter answers 409, a case under hold refuses the movement, and nothing changes and no decision record is written in either refusal. The local projection that answers the closure fact is kept minimal and is not specified by any source.
why: The legacy criterion starts from the data and the rule version being in place, the FSD A2.19 has no alternate flow, the TSD P6 has no state machine of its own, and R-UNI-20 names the legal hold without naming the action it blocks for an original; the values are therefore a parameter and a consumed fact rather than code.
